name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3275
preamble: Joshua Kosman and Henri Picciotto Share Copy Link Facebook X (Twitter) Bluesky Pocket Email March 12, 2013 This article appears in the April 1, 2013 issue.

clue.text: End angst — jump wildly for spur-of-the-moment decision

indicators.note: doing something wildly means doing it without order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Advice to stop worrying by leaping into action without thinking things through.
explanation.walkthrough: JUDGMENT is the American spelling, without the E after the G. SNAP is also one of the three Rice Krispies sounds that make up this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap judgment is an idiom for a verdict reached instantly, without reflection or deliberation.

clue.text: Latin American dictator is the first to wear orange, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the result comes out unexpectedly, so the letters are rearranged
here the first letter is put on along with the colour word before the whole is mixed

blocks.note: its first letter
the colour, taken whole

explanation.surface: A dictator is the first to dress in orange, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel Noriega was the military ruler of Panama in the 1980s, deposed by a US invasion.

clue.text: Part of a setting in ascent to conquer face of Chilean mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue an ascent means reading upwards, so the pieces are taken in reverse
a face is the front, so only the opening letter of the country's adjective is used

blocks.note: to tame is to subdue or conquer
its first letter
an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: Climbers ascend to conquer the face of a peak in Chile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of a setting' sounds like a stage or landscape, but it is a table setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A place mat is one item laid at each diner's position when a table is set.

clue.text: One fleeing during a game of tag?

definitions.text: fleeing during a game of tag?

blocks.note: first meaning: a single thing, a one

blocks.clueFragment: fleeing during a game of tag?
blocks.note: second meaning, punning: in tag whoever runs away is not the chaser

explanation.walkthrough: In the children's game tag, the chaser is called 'it'; anyone running away is therefore un-it, and the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single whole thing, so it can stand for the number one.

clue.text: Turn into particles from the moon, coming up through an opening

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means rising, so the Latin word for the moon reads upwards
passing through something puts you inside it, so the moon word sits within the opening

blocks.note: a grate is a grating over an opening
Luna is the Latin name for the moon

explanation.surface: Dust from the moon rising up through a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To granulate is to form into grains, small particles such as sugar crystals.

clue.text: Overhangs cut the top off foliage

indicators.note: cutting the top off a down entry removes its first letter

blocks.note: leaves are a plant's foliage

explanation.surface: Pruning instructions: trim the topmost greenery from overhanging branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaves are the lower edges of a roof that project beyond the walls.

clue.text: Unfortunately, it ain't a fairy queen

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so these letters have gone astray and need rearranging

blocks.note: all seven letters, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A disappointed child is told that the visitor is not a fairy queen after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Communists originally torment Walesa in Eastern Silesia with glazed pottery

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the opening letter of the word
in an across-read word the east is the right-hand end, so the last letter

blocks.note: its first letter
to rack is to torment, as on the rack
Lech Walesa, the Polish union leader and president
taken as written
its last letter

explanation.surface: Communist authorities persecute Lech Walesa in Silesia while the fine porcelain looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: CRACKLE is one of the three Rice Krispies sounds in this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackle china has a glaze deliberately covered in a network of fine cracks, a decorative ceramic finish.

clue.text: Agent returning California bread for each individual

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word for agent is read from right to left

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
CA is the postal abbreviation for California
pita is a flat Middle Eastern bread (pitta in Britain)

explanation.surface: A sales rep heads back to California with a bread delivery for every customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Per capita is Latin for 'by heads', the standard phrase for an amount counted per person.

clue.text: Tree-hugging union with source concealing head of radical leftist coalition

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap your arms round, so the tree word surrounds the next letter
to conceal something is to hide it inside, so the source word holds the next letter
the head is the top, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the poplar is a tall tree
U is a standard abbreviation for union
a font is a spring or source
its first letter

explanation.surface: Tree-hugging activists, unions and radicals form a broad left alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: POP is the third Rice Krispies sound of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A Popular Front is a historical term for an alliance of left-wing parties against fascism.

clue.text: Elector's trove relocated

indicators.note: relocated means moved elsewhere, so the letters of the word are shifted into new places

blocks.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's hidden stash of treasure has been moved to a new spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; it is not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is anyone entitled to cast a ballot, which is what a voter does.

clue.text: Irritated by Delaware, Joe Biden makes a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the whole string so far is read backwards

blocks.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware
Biden was then Vice President, informally the Veep

explanation.surface: A political story: Biden, Delaware's own senator, staging a return despite annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: Biden represented Delaware in the Senate and was Vice President when this puzzle ran in 2013.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeved is an informal synonym for annoyed or vexed.

clue.text: Wayward cousin limiting nonsense: "Not so fast!"

indicators.note: wayward means straying from the proper path, so these letters stray out of their order
to limit is to set bounds on, so the shuffled word encloses the other piece

blocks.note: the six letters to be shuffled, split around the insert
BS is the American abbreviation for bull, meaning nonsense

explanation.surface: A rebellious cousin talking rubbish is told to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: the exclamation reads as a cry of caution, but it describes something whose speed is below that of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsonic describes speeds below the speed of sound, so not as fast as a supersonic craft.

clue.text: Misdirect TA: "Yard sale is off"

indicators.note: something that is off is wrong or out of kilter, so the letters are in the wrong order and need rearranging

blocks.note: every letter of these words is the raw material

explanation.surface: A teaching assistant mistakenly announces that a garage sale has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is a teaching assistant; a yard sale is the American name for selling household goods in your front yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead astray is an idiom meaning to steer someone the wrong way, literally or morally.

clue.text: For this puzzle, 27 stop the car where a roller coaster might be found

definitions.text: where a roller coaster might be found

blocks.note: the answer to 27 across supplies this puzzle's unifying idea
to park is to stop and leave a car

explanation.surface: A cross-reference in which the cereal at 27 sets the puzzle's tone, then an instruction to pull over.
explanation.walkthrough: Rice Krispies' sounds, Snap, Crackle and Pop, start 1 across, 8 down and 9 down, so the cereal is this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement parks built around a theme are typical homes for roller coasters and other rides.

clue.text: Bird's means of transportation

blocks.note: first meaning: a marsh bird of the crake family
second meaning: the railway as a way of moving goods and people

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive, making it sound like a bird's way of getting about, but it is short for 'is' and joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a wading bird related to the coot and travel by train.

clue.text: Prepares for surgery (brush first, eat later)

blocks.note: to scrub is to brush hard
to sup is to eat supper

explanation.surface: A daily routine: brush your teeth first and have something to eat later.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket gives the order of the two pieces: the brushing word comes first, the eating word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons scrub up, washing hands and arms thoroughly before operating.

clue.text: Capital is more corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or debased, so the word's letters are damaged into a new order

blocks.note: the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that the seat of government is the most crooked place.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital city of Italy, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Senate majority leader cut short stupid uprising? That's not so clear

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its tail, so the final letter of the word for stupid goes
in a down clue an uprising means going up, so everything is read bottom to top

blocks.note: Harry Reid led the US Senate majority in 2013
dumb is American slang for stupid

explanation.surface: A senator's foolish revolt leaves the political picture murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddier water is cloudier, and figuratively a muddier situation is more confused, less clear.

clue.text: Observed from a distance, subject captivating the European Community about the French

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to take captive, so the first word holds the next pieces inside it
about means around, so the pair of letters for the community wraps round the French article

blocks.note: a topic is a subject of discussion
EC is the abbreviation for the European Community
les is the French plural for 'the'

explanation.surface: A distant observer studies a topic involving Europe and France.
explanation.walkthrough: The two containers nest: 'about' works on the community and the French article first, and only then does 'captivating' place that unit inside the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Telescopic sights or views are those seen through a telescope, from far off.

clue.text: Vegetables for Mussolini?

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
Il Duce was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: What a fascist dictator might have had on his plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'for Mussolini' is to be read as 'in favour of the Duce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce is the usual American grocer's word for fresh fruit and vegetables.

clue.text: Dissolute lord to maintain former tennis champion

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, and a loosened word falls into a different order

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
to aver is to maintain or assert as true

explanation.surface: A debauched aristocrat insists on something about an old tennis star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolute lord' looks like a description of a rake; 'dissolute' is only the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Laver is the Australian player who won two calendar Grand Slams, in 1962 and 1969.

clue.text: Minnesota DH occasionally covers for these circumstances

indicators.note: the phrase before it covers the answer, holding it inside a run of its letters

blocks.note: the run straddles the end of the state, the two-letter abbreviation and the start of the adverb

explanation.surface: A Minnesota Twins designated hitter sometimes fills in for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' looks like an alternate-letters signal but is just part of the hiding place. DH is baseball's designated hitter, who bats in place of the pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this', meaning arranged for a particular purpose or situation only.

clue.text: In retrospect, one person embraces family rating for horror movie star

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the whole build is read from its end to its start
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the word for a person holds the rating letter

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'
G is the US film rating for general, family audiences

explanation.surface: Looking back, a lone moviegoer picks a family film over a horror star's work.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUL takes G inside it to make SOGUL, I goes in front, and the whole string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Lugosi was the Hungarian-born actor famous for playing Dracula in the 1931 film.

clue.text: Fruit is oddly un-Gallic

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: its first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A fruit is said to be strangely un-French.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine with wrinkled skin.

clue.text: It's heard in stable sounds, like rejection

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is pronounced the same as the word that follows

blocks.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal

explanation.surface: Noises in a stable that come across as a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable sounds' wants to be the definition, but 'sounds' belongs with 'like' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry of a horse, which is what one hears in a stable.

clue.text: Argonauts mixed bitters

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Jason's crew of heroes mixing up a cocktail ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed bitters' reads as a cocktail phrase, but 'mixed' acts on the heroes' name before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura is the best-known brand of aromatic bitters, used in cocktails.

clue.text: Recklessly, I risk recipes for breakfast food

indicators.note: acting recklessly means without care, so the letters are scattered into a careless new order

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these words

explanation.surface: A cook gambles on untried recipes for the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice Krispies is a Kellogg's cereal of puffed rice, eaten in the morning with milk.
